title: Engineering Practices
intro: Engineering practices questions test how a candidate collaborates, makes architectural decisions, and manages technical debt — the non-coding skills that determine whether a mid-level engineer grows into a senior one. Code review at Rails shops follows the same principle as anywhere: anchor on intent first (is this solving the right problem?), architecture second (is the abstraction right?), style last (RuboCop handles this). ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) are the structured format for capturing why a decision was made — context, decision, consequences — especially valuable in Rails codebases where a choice between service objects and concerns made three years ago has compounding effects. Technical debt in Rails typically accumulates in fat models, skipped database indexes, and test suites that use create when build_stubbed would do.
